n: David hears that the Philistines are attacking Keilah, a Judean town, and stealing grain from its threshing floors at harvest time.

f.g: A fortified town in the Judean lowlands, a few miles south of Adullam.
where harvested grain was processed — stealing it meant famine

n: Unlike Saul, David asks the Lord before acting. The Lord tells him to go and save Keilah. Even as a fugitive, David acts as Israel's protector.
David's men are afraid: they're already scared hiding in Judah, so how much worse to fight the Philistine army?
David asks the Lord again, and receives a clear promise of victory. Seeking confirmation to strengthen others' faith is wise leadership.

f.w: I will deliver the Philistines into thine hand

n: David and his men defeat the Philistines, take their livestock, and rescue Keilah's people.
A note explains that Abiathar brought the ephod with him when he fled. This sacred garment, with the Urim and Thummim, let David inquire of the Lord.

f.g: The high priest's ephod with its breastplate held the Urim and Thummim used to receive revelation.

n: Saul hears David is in Keilah and thinks God has delivered him into his hands — a walled town would trap him. Saul misreads God's will completely.
Saul calls up his army to march on Keilah and besiege David — attacking a town David had just rescued.
David learns of Saul's plot and asks Abiathar to bring the ephod so he can seek the Lord's guidance.
David prays, telling the Lord he has heard Saul plans to destroy the city because of him.
David asks two questions: will Keilah's people hand him over, and will Saul come? The Lord answers the second first: Saul will come.
David asks again whether Keilah's people will betray him, and the Lord says yes. The town he saved would hand him over to save itself.

f.g: This shows God's knowledge of what would happen under certain conditions.

n: David's band, now about six hundred, leaves Keilah and keeps moving. When Saul hears David has escaped, he calls off the march.
David hides in strongholds in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul hunts him every day, but God does not let Saul find him.

f.g: Rugged desert hills southeast of Hebron.

f.w: God delivered him not into his hand

n: David knows Saul has come out to kill him, and he stays hidden in a wooded area at Ziph.
Jonathan secretly visits David and “strengthened his hand in God” — he encourages David's faith. True friends point us to the Lord.
Jonathan tells David not to fear: Saul won't find him, David will be king, and Jonathan will be second to him. Even Saul knows it. Jonathan humbly accepts God's plan for David.

f.w: thou shalt be king over Israel

n: They renew their covenant before the Lord. Jonathan returns home and David stays in the woods. This is the last time the two friends meet.

f.w: made a covenant before the LORD

n: The people of Ziph go to Saul and betray David's hiding place in the hill of Hachilah. The heading of Psalm 54 refers to this betrayal.

f.g: “The wasteland,” the barren desert near the Dead Sea.

n: They urge Saul to come whenever he wants, promising to hand David over.
Saul blesses them in the Lord's name and praises their “compassion” on him — a twisted use of religious language for a murderous goal.
Saul asks them to gather more detailed information on David's location and who has seen him, since David is known to be very clever.

f.g: Literally “where his foot is” — where he goes.

n: Saul wants every hiding place mapped out. Then he will come and search all the clans of Judah to find David.
The Ziphites go ahead of Saul, but David and his men have moved to the wilderness of Maon, farther south.

f.g: A town and desert area south of Ziph.

n: Saul pursues. David, warned, goes down to a rocky hill in the wilderness of Maon, and Saul follows him there.
Saul's forces are on one side of the mountain and David's on the other. Saul's men are closing in from both sides — David is nearly trapped.
At the last moment a messenger arrives: the Philistines are raiding the land! The timing shows God's protecting hand.
Saul breaks off the chase to fight the Philistines. The place is named Sela-hammahlekoth, “rock of escape” or “rock of division.”

f.g: Hebrew “rock of parting” or “rock of escape.”

n: David moves to the strongholds of En-gedi, an oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea with springs and caves.

f.g: “Spring of the young goat,” a lush oasis surrounded by cliffs.
